answer.rationale: Constraints do most of the pruning. The line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so any path that interrupts or re-qualifies primary supply inside two weeks raises delivery risk and violates the stated objective. That rules out switch_primary_vendor as this cycle's single move (memory_c2's 'quick onboarding' was recorded under unknown volume slack and is a year stale) and rules out defer_decision (memory_c5 worked because that renewal was non-critical and continued month-to-month; here the primary contract simply expires). add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right structural fix for single-point-of-failure but delivers little of the mandated 18% this year and does not by itself keep primary supply alive past day 85. renew_incumbent as-is (memory_c1) protects delivery but concedes the cost mandate outright. That leaves negotiate_terms: memory_c4 says benchmarking moved this incumbent on price and payment terms at renewal, and memory_c6 says term length was a lever that cut unit cost without narrowing scope. The incumbent has refused to reopen price 'this cycle' — a renewal is a different negotiation surface than a mid-cycle reopen, and term structure, payment terms, and volume banding are levers that do not require them to reverse that refusal. So I verify the two memories my plan actually leans on: memory_c6 (is the multi-year-for-volume-price mechanism real, and what did it cost in flexibility?) and memory_c2 (is the low-cost vendor's delta large and current enough to be credible benchmark leverage, and was it the same component class?). I did not verify memory_c4 because its claim is directionally reinforced by c6 and it is the weaker of the two dependencies; if c6's source shows the volume pricing came bundled with commitments I cannot make at 94% utilization, my plan degrades to a short bridge renewal plus a second-source qualification next cycle rather than a multi-year lock. Scale is a standard experiment, not a broad rollout: I will not sign a long multi-year commitment on inherited summaries alone, because a term lock plus a sole incumbent compounds the exact single-point-of-failure memory_c3 was written about, and locking multi-year now forecloses the second-source and vendor-switch options that later reviews may need. Residual uncertainty is real: none of these memories carries the volume-slack, component-scope, or counterparty context that would tell me whether the recorded outcomes transfer, and I may not reach the full 18% by terms alone — partial capture plus preserved optionality is the better trade than a full-cut gamble against a line with no buffer.
